[Back to the project overview](../README.md) ·
[Methods](../docs/methods.md) · [Results](../docs/results.md)

This scenario integrates uncertainty in the baseline contact graph: every
replicate draws a separate Watts--Strogatz network, while every engine uses the
same graph for a given replicate.

## Model

The [common model](../docs/methods.md#common-model) with no interventions, on
Watts–Strogatz networks with mean degree 20 and rewiring probability 0.05, at
10,000 and 100,000 agents. Each engine runs 100 replicates per size; a
deterministic, separately cached graph is generated for every size/replicate
pair and shared across engines for that pair.

```{r}
#| label: parameters
table_parameters(bench)
```

## Engine notes

Every engine runs its baseline implementation, described in
[Engines](../docs/methods.md#engines). The three epiworld runners build the
same model and, in this scenario, produce identical epidemics for every seed.

### Time to a first result

*Build* turns the edge list into the engine's model, once per network (and thus
once per replicate in this scenario);
*build + simulate* is the time to a first result once the edge list is in
memory ([Timing](../docs/methods.md#timing)).

## Notes

**Calibration.** All engines initially run with multiplier 1.0. Scenario 00's
factors were estimated on a fixed degree-10 graph and are not valid for this
degree-20, graph-varying design. A later calibration will estimate factors
against this scenario's 100 network draws before any calibrated results are
published.

**Model lines.** They vary with how much of the model an engine provides.
EoN describes transitions as rate graphs, Covasim overrides its native
parameters to restrict itself to SEIRH, Starsim subclasses its SEIR for the
hospital state, the ixa, individual, and Agents.jl runners write their
daily step or infection process by hand, and the EpiModel runner writes its
infection, progression, and prevalence modules. The FRED runner's lines are the
Python that writes FRED's model file and population.
